brief: A brass lamp sits on the shelf, waiting to be useful.
description: A brass carbide lamp, dented, honest, and heavier than it looks. It has clearly been down a hole before and has come back every time.

brief: A flask of lamp oil leans in the corner.
description: A flat tin flask, three-quarters full of oil. It sloshes with the particular smugness of a thing you will need later.

brief: A dented tin cup hangs from a nail.
description: A tin cup, dented, tea-stained, and worth precisely nothing. It is here to be confused with better things.
Split from root to shoulder. The hollow inside is dark, dry, and exactly the shape of somewhere people hide things.
A stubby iron key gone orange with rust. The teeth are still good, which is the only part that has to be.

brief: A steel grate is set into the floor.
description: Steel bars in a steel frame, bolted into the rock and fitted with a lock that has outlived whoever turned it last.

brief: A carving has been cut beneath the water.
description: Letters cut deep beneath the running water, worn soft at the edges but perfectly readable. Something has been scratched around them, later and in more of a hurry.
readText: SAY ZEEBLE AND THE HILL FORGETS THE DISTANCE. IT WORKS BOTH WAYS. THAT IS THE PART PEOPLE FORGET.

brief: A rusted door lies flat in the floor.
description: An iron door set flush into the grotto floor, so thoroughly rusted that door and floor have reached an understanding. The hinges want oil more than they want anything.

brief: A silver chalice stands in a niche, catching the moss-light.
description: A silver chalice, tarnished to the colour of weather. Whoever left it here did not leave it as an offering; they left it because it was heavy and they were in a hurry.

brief: A small wooden box sits against the wall.
description: A box of black wood, banded in iron, with a keyhole that has been waiting a long time for company.

brief: A jade idol squats in the box, looking pleased with itself.
description: A squat jade figure with its hands on its knees, carved by someone who had never seen the thing they were carving and was not going to let that stop them.
